title: Island Editor
idea: A browser dev tool where a developer builds an island by placing objects and NPCs, giving each NPC a quest, and setting the background color and ground sections, then saves it as a versioned JSON file.

glossary.meaning: A dev-only page in the browser for building one island's layout visually instead of typing coordinates into islands.ts.
A developer on the team (not a player) who uses the editor.
A PlacedObject: an entry from the object catalog (objects.ts, e.g. palm-tree, volcano) placed at a world position with a scale and an optional sign.
A character on the island (Shuto, Jordi, Tiffany, Genki, Sarah...) with a position and dialog from npcs/dialogs/<npc>.json.
The quest an NPC offers when the player talks to it; today this is matched by kana to a row in the Supabase quests table.
The island's base ground color (ISLAND_BG), shown wherever no section covers the world.
A BgSection: a full-width ground band (e.g. volcano, forest, beach, ocean) with its own color and a border to the next band.
The island in a phone-sized frame at real game zoom, where touch walks the player around to test it.
The island's number (islands.id), e.g. 1 for the tropical island.
A version number that goes up by one with each save of the same island: 1_ver1.json, 1_ver2.json, ...
The editor's palette of placeable things, grouped in folder dropdowns: npcs/, tiles/ (the tile path, GitHub issue #6) and objects/.
The lesson level a quest belongs to, e.g. vocab or meaning.
Which quest game runs, e.g. dodge or door.
What the quest tests: a kana for dodge, or answer + decoy words for door.
The y coordinate where the dithered border line between a section and the one above it is drawn.

features.name: Object placement
features.whatItDoes: Pick an object from the catalog and place it on the island.
details: Writes PlacedObject data: def, x, y, scale, optional sign interaction.
An asset box lists everything placeable in folder dropdowns: asset box / npcs / and asset box / objects /.
Pick an item in the asset box, click the canvas to drop it, drag it to move it.
A side panel shows the selected item's x, y, scale and sign text for fine-tuning.
The selected item can be deleted (Delete key or button) or duplicated (copy placed next to it).
The selected sprite can be scaled on the canvas (drag a corner handle) as well as by the scale field in the side panel.

features.name: NPC placement
details: NPCs come from the asset box's npcs/ folder and are placed and moved the same way as objects (click to drop, drag, side panel).

features.name: Quest per NPC
features.whatItDoes: Choose which quest each NPC offers.
details: The side panel has a quest dropdown for the selected NPC, plus the quest's props.
Quests can be created and edited in the side panel; they are saved to the Supabase quests table.
Quest props: level (e.g. vocab, meaning), quest type (e.g. dodge, door) and target.
Target shape depends on the quest: a kana string for dodge (target: あ), or { answer: [...], decoys: [...] } for door (answer: 食べる, 歩く, 走る; decoys: 食べる, 歩く, 走る, 行く, 寝る).
Island and quest props are loaded from Supabase.

features.name: Background and sections
features.whatItDoes: Set the island's base color and its ground sections (separations).
details: Sections are an ordered array, top to bottom; each has start (y), end (y), color and separator (y).
separator is the y where the dithered border line between this section and the one above is drawn; it can differ from start.
start is optional: left out, it is 0 for the first section or the end of the section above.
The base bg color shows where no section covers the world.

features.name: Desktop / phone view switch
features.whatItDoes: The editor is laid out for a desktop browser; a button switches the canvas to a phone-browser view.
details: Phone view shows the island in a phone-sized frame at real game zoom.
In phone view, touch drives the game controls: the dev walks the player around to test the island.

features.name: Versioned save
features.whatItDoes: Saving writes the island to island-editor/<island_index>_ver<N>.json, with N one higher than the last save.
details: Saving works on the deployed Vercel site.
Files go to a Supabase Storage bucket named island-editor: <island_index>_ver<N>.json, N one higher than the highest.
The game fetches the newest version of an island, replacing the hand-written map in islands.ts.

features.name: Open a version
features.whatItDoes: When the editor opens, the dev picks an island and any of its saved versions to start editing from.
details: Saving always writes a new ver (one higher than the highest), never overwrites the opened one.

features.name: Open access
features.whatItDoes: The editor page opens for anyone with the URL, without login, like /Dev.
details: Anyone who opens it can save new versions and create or edit quests.

features.name: Sprite upload
features.whatItDoes: Upload a new sprite image so it appears in asset box / objects/ and can be placed.
details: The uploaded image is stored both in this repo (alongside the other sprites in public/img/) and in Supabase.

features.name: Undo / redo
features.whatItDoes: Step back and forward through edits made in the current editing session.
details: Covers placing, moving, scaling, deleting, duplicating, quest and section changes.

flows.name: Edit an island
steps: Open the editor in a desktop browser.
Pick an island and one of its saved versions; the editor loads it (and its quests) from Supabase.
Open asset box / objects/ or npcs/, pick an item, click the canvas to drop it, drag to move, fine-tune x, y, scale and sign in the side panel.
Select an NPC and pick or create its quest: level, quest type, target.
Set the bg color and the sections (start, end, color, separator).
Press the phone-view button and walk the player around with touch / game controls to check it.
Save: a new <island_index>_ver<N>.json is written to the island-editor bucket.
The game now loads that newest version for the island.

examples.situation: Island 1 has saved 1_ver1 and 1_ver2; the dev opens 1_ver1, moves a palm tree and saves.
examples.whatHappens: 1_ver3.json is written; 1_ver1 and 1_ver2 stay; the game loads 1_ver3.

examples.situation: The dev places Shuto and gives him a quest with level vocab, quest type dodge, target あ.
examples.whatHappens: The quest is saved to the quests table and Shuto offers it on the island.

examples.situation: The dev gives Jordi a door quest with answer 食べる, 歩く, 走る and decoys 食べる, 歩く, 走る, 行く, 寝る.
examples.whatHappens: The quest's target is stored as { answer, decoys } and the door quest uses those words.

examples.situation: Sections: beach with no start and end 1700, then ocean with end 2000 and separator 1690.
examples.whatHappens: Beach starts at 0; ocean starts at 1700 (end of the beach) and its dithered border is drawn at y 1690.

leftOut: Editing hitboxes: objects keep the catalog's hitbox.
Creating new NPCs or writing their dialog in the editor.

decisions.decision: The spec lives in docs/island-editor.spec.json, not the repo root.
Saved files are named <island_index>_ver<N>.json inside an island-editor folder.
The game loads the saved JSON for an island instead of the hand-written islands.ts map.
The island-editor folder is at the repo root.
Placing: asset box with npcs/ and objects/ folder dropdowns, click to drop, drag to move, side panel for exact values.
The editor opens any saved version of an island, chosen by the dev.
Each NPC gets a quest from a dropdown, with props level, quest type and target.
Sections: ordered array of { start?, end, color, separator }; start defaults to 0 or the end of the section above.
Saving must work on Vercel; island and quest props load from Supabase.
decisions.reason: Supersedes the repo-file part of D-3/D-4: a deployed site can't write repo files.

decisions.decision: Phone view is a phone-sized preview frame at game zoom, with touch interaction.
Saved versions are files in a Supabase Storage bucket named island-editor.
Quests are created and edited in the editor and saved to the Supabase quests table.
A section's separator is the y of its dithered border line.
Touch in phone view is the game's controls (walk the player), not editing.
Anyone can open the editor and save, no login.
Out of v1: sprite upload, undo/redo. In: delete + duplicate, hitbox editing, creating NPCs and dialog.
v1 includes sprite upload, undo/redo and scaling sprites on the canvas; hitbox editing and creating NPCs/dialog are left out.
decisions.reason: Corrects D-16, which had them the wrong way round.

decisions.decision: Uploaded sprites are stored in this repo and in Supabase.

assumptions.statement: Saving always creates a new ver file; older versions are kept.
Sprite upload asks for a key (a-z, 0-9, -), prefilled from the file name, and a world size w / h, prefilled from the image's own size; uploaded sprites have no hitbox.
The repo copy of an uploaded sprite (public/img/uploads/) is written only when the editor runs under npm run dev; on Vercel the upload goes to the Supabase sprites bucket only.
Sections also carry optional solid and wave flags, so a saved island 1 keeps its blocking, moving ocean.
The game reads each quest's target (kana) but still runs every quest as dodge, the only quest in this demo.

openQuestions.question: Sprite upload: what is set on upload (name, world size w/h)?
Sprite upload on the deployed Vercel site can't write into the repo: does the repo copy happen only when running locally, or is it synced into the repo another way?
